business_rules.statement: Tenants may only make the platform stricter than default and never looser than the platform floor, with rejection rather than logging; seven platform-fixed items are named.
business_rules.applies_to: All five surfaces, every role including the root

business_rules.statement: No artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path; detection is rule-based and runs on the worker's device using packaged limits and mappings.
business_rules.enforcement_point: On-device deterministic layer; atom registration declares side-effects

business_rules.statement: Fixed Severity 1 floor: automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation; on-device classification including offline; weakening the floor is Explicitly prohibited.
business_rules.enforcement_point: On-device classification at instant of capture; registry rejects weakening

business_rules.statement: Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly; supervisors may request release with a note and nothing more.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Client Command Center operational action 4, executed through the owning Hub service

business_rules.statement: Specification gates are hard and always; the evaluation gate is hard and always including for the root account; the qualification gate is the only configurable gate, with strict blocking as its default.
business_rules.applies_to: All five surfaces, all nine human security role types

business_rules.statement: The safety layer is not configurable and has no off switch, including under a platform-wide emergency pause.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Frontline native execution core; emergency pause governs agents only

business_rules.statement: The creator of a Job can never approve the same Job; routing finds a second approver. Segregation of duties is absolute and enforced by routing, not by policy.
Nothing reaches a worker without explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer and Release Authority; the Reviewer must be a different person from the Author and cannot edit.
business_rules.applies_to: SURF-STU, all authored content including AI-drafted levels and locale variants

business_rules.statement: The Client Command Center action set is closed at exactly ten actions; four things are absolutely prohibited for every role: gate override, pausing/stopping a run, editing any record or configuration, creating Jobs or runs.
business_rules.enforcement_point: `§6.14.2` and `§6.14.3`; every action is a command through the owning Hub service
business_rules.applies_to: Every role on SURF-CC including the Quality Manager

business_rules.statement: Six enforced invariants bind every account including the root, with no approval path around them; the eight-row platform floor register rejects rather than logs.
business_rules.applies_to: SURF-SA and all four tenant-facing surfaces

business_rules.statement: Nothing is purged. The retention value is a hot-retrievability horizon defaulting to fifteen years; deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: `MOD-SA-17` Data Lifecycle and Archival; retention change is critical-class

business_rules.statement: Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act: worker personal data anonymises at twenty-four months for standard tenants; never in Regulated-Industry mode.
One immutable append-only audit log per tenant, committing in the same transaction as the action it records; no delete or edit path exists on any surface for any account.
Package pinning: a run finishes on the version it started on; in-flight runs are never re-based.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Work package pinned per run at assignment

business_rules.statement: No worker-facing pace of any kind, ever — no pace figure, timer, or comparison in any module, state, or release of this scope.
Runtime machine translation is Explicitly prohibited in all four localisation layers; a publish-time locale completeness check blocks publication in an incomplete locale.
Composing action agents is Explicitly prohibited at launch; the Agent Author capability is tier-gated to Growth and Enterprise and Unavailable on Starter.
Enabling a capability with pending or failing evaluation scenarios is Explicitly prohibited for every account; the eval gate has no off position.
Presenting stale data as current is Explicitly prohibited; every tile and drill view carries a compact sync-state element listing devices and last-seen times.
A skew-flagged write cannot win a conflict unreviewed and is excluded from bulk acceptance; beyond the skew threshold ordering follows server receipt.
Naming individuals in an escalation routing template is Explicitly prohibited; templates name roles, never individuals.
Muting in-app notifications is Explicitly prohibited; three always-firing event families cannot be disabled; users mute digest sections, never services.
Editing a summary is Explicitly prohibited; corrections are append-only annotations, and a material change after finish triggers an audited recompute preserving the prior output.
Wipe without a final sync attempt is Explicitly prohibited; sync-then-wipe is a critical-class action mirrored to both audit trails.
Standing JBS access is Explicitly prohibited; every JBS touch is a scoped, time-boxed, reason-linked, audited and mirrored grant that expires.
Ambient browsing of tenant content is Explicitly prohibited; exactly three named access classes exist — support session, compliance-emergency path, JBS access grant.
Cross-tenant sharing of learned material is Explicitly prohibited; strict tenant isolation with no external training data.
Comparative cross-tenant analytics are anonymised aggregates enforced as an invariant; the telemetry module carries counts, rates and statuses only, no operational content.
Worker self-assignment is Explicitly prohibited; assignment is supervisor-driven with a qualification check and unlimited concurrency with per-individual attribution.
Exactly two in-flight run modifications are permitted: worker substitution and capped end-time extension.
Price metadata on a tier record is Explicitly prohibited; pricing, invoicing and payment sit entirely outside the platform.
business_rules.enforcement_point: `MOD-SA-11` Tiers, Entitlements and Caps; Part XI Block 6

business_rules.statement: The Delivery Operations Hub runs no live agents at all and originates no operational data; the Frontline Worker Application is the only place operational data is created.
Structural re-parenting of a location while in-flight Jobs exist is Explicitly prohibited; archive-and-recreate is the sanctioned path. Name and address edits are always allowed.
Editing a shift never retroactively re-stamps completed runs.
Media never touches the device gallery; evidence is immutable at creation and bound to step, unit, identity, device and both timestamps.
Named-location provenance is a named site, line and cell, never a coordinate, never a gate, disclosed plainly to the worker.
Interrupting an in-flight run with a work-instruction change notice is Explicitly prohibited; the notified tier is presented at the start of the next execution.
Blocking a shift start on handoff-brief acknowledgement is Explicitly prohibited; an unacknowledged brief flags after a default thirty-minute grace period.
Required feedback is Explicitly prohibited; feedback is optional, one tap, and never gating.
A default per-worker live wall is Explicitly prohibited; the board shows cells and lines, and worker-level detail is reachable only by drilling from an exception.
Custom role creation is Explicitly prohibited at V1; five fixed tenant roles, four fixed console roles, additive multi-role with identity-based audit.
At least one Tenant Admin must exist, and an approver must exist whenever a Job exists (two mandatory-role rules); delegation is deferred.
Atom authoring is Explicitly prohibited to every tenant; atoms arrive by backend migration and there is no console create flow.
Genealogy at launch is one level of as-built links plus full rework history; no multi-level walkable genealogy is claimed.
Severity is never a workflow default; it must be mapped per screen, explicitly, on every screen that can deviate.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Workflow Builder (`§5.4.1`) and screen configuration section 7 (`§5.5.8`)

business_rules.statement: A soft proof gate never softens the specification gate; configuring away an out-of-tolerance deviation is Explicitly prohibited.
Training Library content is online-only, excluded from the offline package, produces no production record, and never substitutes for a qualification.
Automatic execution of an undecided gate item is Explicitly prohibited; an item never executes on its own and never silently expires.
Lane B changes are never auto-approved but are automatically published; auto-approval is Explicitly prohibited and Lane B always requires a person.
An escalation resolving to nobody is Explicitly prohibited; escalation resolves to on-shift holders of the routed role with a marked Quality Manager fallback.
Practice mode is cut, not deferred; it returns only as a change request.

contradictions.description: Record-finish bounds are open drafting values in §2.4 and settled in §4.6.8 and §8.19.

contradictions.description: submitted and complete defined differently in three Parts: per-worker device event (§2.4) vs run-level state on lodged captures (§4.6.8) vs run-level on device sync (§6.2.6).

contradictions.description: A manually closed stuck run is complete at close time (§2.4) but stands submitted with the gap recorded (§6.2.6).

submitted with the gap recorded, finish window still guarantees it finishes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Inherited by every section of Chapter 5, the Source Coverage Map

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Section-specific
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Coverage reported lower with the reason, never higher
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-issue of the affected chapter and recomputation of Section 5.13

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The map is complete forwards but unusable backwards because blueprint statements were not tagged with their locators

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Affected chapter re-read against the source Part and its claims re-classified
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Claims that cannot be traced are re-labelled `Assumption` and listed for client confirmation, never presented as contracted requirements
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-issue of the affected chapter with classifications restored

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Sideways walk returns every locator for the theme regardless of layer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Layer 1 statement governs, because the platform-wide contract is what no surface may fork
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-read the Layer 1 Part in full

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A locator printed one way in Table A and another way in Table B so the halves no longer join
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Match on the source heading text instead of the locator
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Re-issue both halves of the affected Part together from a single enumeration pass
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Part is reported as unreconciled in Section 5.13, lowering reported coverage rather than hiding the break

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The §1.7 row is authoritative and the divergent chapter is corrected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where §1.7 itself conflicts with a surface Part, the decision identifier governs and both readings are preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The three closing states are named identically in Parts II, IV and VI but defined with different trigger conditions
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: DEC-RUNSTATE-001 is cited wherever the states are used and both readings are carried
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The blueprint uses the Part II definition as the platform-wide contract and marks every use with the identifier
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No chapter asserts a single settled definition

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A later Part appearing to grant an agent or a role more than Part III allows

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Part III reading is treated as governing for design purposes and the divergence escalated as a client decision
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The stricter of the two readings is designed to, so no build ships an authority the source may not have granted

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A Hub module referenced by a name that does not match the §4.1.3 inventory

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A capability appearing in no inventory row is recorded as unhomed and raised as a scope question

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The derived eighteen-module Studio model quoted elsewhere as a source-backed count

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The count is removed and the sections referenced by locator alone

failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: V1 scope stands as the source defines it

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A total that includes an extraction artifact or double-counts a heading

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The affected Part's counts are marked unreconciled and reported as such
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The summary reports a lower coverage figure with the reason, never a higher one

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A design chapter carrying nine of nineteen modules or nine of ten actions
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The missing rows are restored from the source table
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The affected chapter is re-issued from the source table rather than from its own previous draft
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The source table is quoted in full in the carrying chapter

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An open item disappearing from a chapter because a plausible answer was written into the prose
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The identifier is restored and the value marked `TBD — Client Decision Required`
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The passage is rewritten to state the options, the recommendation, the trade-offs, and the decision owner
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The value is not stated as contracted anywhere

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A completeness statement that claims product coverage
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The sentence is rewritten with the open-decision count restored
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The statement is reduced to the recountable numbers alone with the open register cited by reference
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The blueprint claims only source coverage

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Terminology drift: an undefined term used in a design chapter; two entries colliding; a worker-facing term drifting between blueprint and locale files
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The term is added to the glossary with its classification and the using chapter left unchanged
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Colliding entries merged or the ambiguous entry split, and every using chapter re-checked
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Where a term cannot be settled, the blueprint uses the source's own wording verbatim and cites the locator, rather than inventing a clearer word
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-issue of Chapter 6 followed by a term sweep of every chapter that used the affected term; reconciliation regenerates the Section 6.12 abbreviation register

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A short form appearing in prose, usually in a table cell where space was tight
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Expand it in place
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The column header carries the full name and the cells carry a defined symbol explained in a legend beneath the table
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The table is split rather than abbreviated, because an unreadable table is a better outcome than an ambiguous one

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A chapter writing that an agent 'decides', 'classifies', 'releases', or 'approves'
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The verb is replaced with the accurate one — proposes, assembles, retrieves, interprets, launches a configured response
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The §3.2 boundary sentence is quoted verbatim in the affected chapter
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No chapter grants an agent authority the source does not

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A chapter describing a platform-fixed behaviour as configurable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The statement is corrected and the §1.5 platform-fixed list restated
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant-configuration registry's rejection behaviour is quoted, making the softening physically impossible rather than merely disallowed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The stricter reading governs the design

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A chapter implying a device received, applied or acknowledged something before it synchronised
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The claim is rewritten against the capture and command state ladders
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The freshness-marker semantics are quoted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The surface says only what it knows, with a timestamp

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A chapter describing a platform touch that is none of the three named classes
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The touch is reclassified into one of the three or removed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: §8.1.2's statement that no ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console is quoted verbatim
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The design carries only three access classes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A chapter writing 'the system retries' or 'a fallback exists' instead of naming a mechanism
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The sentence is rewritten using the named mechanism, its threshold, and its terminal safe state
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The fallback contract identifier is cited and the mechanism specified there
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The design states a controlled hold or safe stop rather than a promise of uninterrupted operation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A dependency starts failing
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Back-off with jitter between retries; after a threshold of consecutive failures the circuit breaker opens and calls stop being attempted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Back-pressure propagates upstream; blast radius assessed as one tenant, one region, or the platform; feature flag switched off or canary release aborted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled hold or safe stop — never a pretence of normal operation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Compensating action undoes partial effect by adding a correcting record rather than deleting anything

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Coaching retrieval fails five times consecutively
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The circuit breaker opens and coaching falls back to the step's authored Work Instructions carried in the package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Client Command Center shows agent unavailability rather than silence
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The deterministic gates, specification checks, severity classification and Severity 1 holds continue untouched on every tablet
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Blast radius assessed; cross-tenant degradation is a platform incident
